analysis: What changed vs the 5 AM brief: the 8:30 AM ET data dump landed and made things worse. Core PCE printed 3.3% y/y (above the 3.2% estimate, highest in three years per WSJ) even though the monthly 0.3% matched forecasts — a September revision pushed the annual rate up. Headline PCE 3.8% matched. Q3 GDP was revised sharply higher to 4.3% vs 3.4% initially, and jobless claims fell to 189k — a hot economy plus hot inflation, which locks in the December hike (CME FedWatch ~99.8% before the print) and keeps January in play. Futures extended losses after the release: S&P -2.1% (was -2.02%), Nasdaq -3.2% (was -3.03%), Dow -1.4%. The AI selloff is now a three-day unwind: Nvidia -5% premarket after -5.86% Tuesday, Monday's +31% Huang rally more than half retraced, and Trump's open-to-an-equity-stake remark (NY Post, single-source) adds a new political overhang. Anthropic is set to fall further below its $83 IPO price. The beat-and-fall earnings pattern continues (Dell, Workday, Ambarella -33%), and the tariff catalyst is still unresolved — WSJ reports hikes planned, USTR has posted nothing. Signal vs noise: the PCE y/y overshoot, the GDP revision, the deepening futures slide and the tariff overhang are signal; any single-name premarket bounce and the exact futures percentages are noise. The open into a thin Thanksgiving-week tape is the risk point.

community_signals.takeaway: r/wallstreetbets daily-discussion analysis reads the mood as capitulation-level pessimism: the community's emerging consensus is that Huang's return does not change AI economics — the worry is returns on AI capex, circular financing and rates, not who the CEO is. It also flags uncorroborated rumors (Treasury hack, Iowa explosive) circulating in the community that searches could not confirm — treat as noise.

headlines.headline: 8:30 AM ET data dump: core PCE +0.3% m/m but 3.3% y/y, above the 3.2% estimate and the highest in three years (a September revision pushed the annual rate up); headline PCE 3.8% y/y as expected. Q3 GDP revised sharply higher to 4.3% vs 3.4% initially; jobless claims fell to 189,000 vs 200,000 expected; durable goods +0.2% vs 0.5% expected. Futures extended losses after the release.
headlines.why_it_matters: Hot inflation plus strong growth locks in the December rate hike and keeps January in play — the Fed has no cover to blink at the selloff, and futures slid further the moment the numbers printed.

headlines.headline: Futures point to a sharply lower open 30 minutes out: Dow -1.4% (nearly 700 points), S&P 500 -2.1%, Nasdaq 100 -3.2%; SPY ETF -2.2%, QQQ -3.2% premarket.
headlines.why_it_matters: The gap-down deepened after the 8:30 data — the open is set to start well below Tuesday's close with tech leading the downside into a thin Thanksgiving-week tape.

headlines.headline: Nvidia -5% premarket after falling 5.86% Tuesday, giving back more than half of Monday's +31% Huang-reinstatement surge. President Trump told the New York Post he is open to Nvidia handing the US government an equity stake — single-source, unconfirmed.
headlines.why_it_matters: The AI unwind is now a three-day story, and a possible government equity stake adds a fresh political overhang — earnings context: Nov 17, EPS $2.68 vs $2.47 expected, revenue $115.84B vs $109.28B expected (+103% y/y). The equity-stake remark is single-source, unconfirmed — treat as fragile.

headlines.headline: White House plans to raise tariffs on goods from China and dozens of other countries, per the Wall Street Journal; USTR Section 301 findings and any rates are still unpublished as of this morning.
headlines.why_it_matters: The market is still selling the tariff headline, not the details — single-source, unconfirmed in substance, so an official USTR posting before or after the open could move futures either way.

headlines.headline: Mega-caps all red premarket: Alphabet -3.5%, Amazon -3.2%, Tesla -2.9%, Meta -2.0%, Microsoft -1.8%; Apple the relative holdout at about -0.5% to -1.0%. Anthropic -5% premarket, set to fall further below its $83 IPO price and ~29% off its recent high.
headlines.why_it_matters: No mega-cap is escaping the slide and the most AI-exposed names are down most; Apple holding up best fits the rotation-into-less-AI-exposed value pattern from Tuesday.

headlines.headline: Earnings movers: Dell -4.7% to -6% despite a record quarter and raised full-year revenue guide to $202B; Workday -5% to -9.9% after beating EPS but guiding Q4 subscription revenue light; Ambarella plunged 33%; Autodesk -5%; HP rose modestly; Deere -2% after its weak FY27 guide.
headlines.why_it_matters: The beat-and-fall pattern from Tuesday is still the rule — even a record quarter with a raised guide is being sold, so the market is judging guidance and valuation, not the quarter.
